author: Chris
description: Photographer James Balog shares new image sequences from the Extreme Ice Survey, a network of time-lapse cameras recording glaciers receding at an alarming rate, some of the most vivid evidence yet of climate change.
title: TED - Time-lapse proof of extreme ice loss; James Balog

author: Chris
description: There's a mistaken belief in today's working world that leaders need to be serious all the time to be taken seriously. The research tells a different story. Based on the course they teach at Stanford's Graduate School of Business, behavioral scientist Jennifer Aaker and corporate strategist Naomi Bagdonas delve into the surprising power of humor: why it's a secret weapon to build bonds, power, creativity and resilience -- and how we can all have more of it.
title: TED - Why great leaders take humor seriously; Jennifer Aaker and Naomi Bagdonas

author: Chris
description: After more than two decades as an anchor for ABC News, an on-air panic attack sent Dan Harris's life in a new direction: he became a dedicated meditator and, to some, even a guru. But then an anonymous survey of his family, friends and colleagues turned up some brutal feedback — he was still kind of a jerk. In a wise, funny talk, he shares his years-long quest to improve his relationships with everyone (starting with himself) and explains the science behind loving-kindness meditation, and how it can boost your resiliency, quiet your inner critic and simply make you more pleasant to be around.
title: TED - The benefits of not being a jerk to yourself; Dan Harris

author: Chris
description: Is it possible for taking action on climate change to make you feel happy? Behavioral scientist Jiaying Zhao believes that's the only way we'll create lasting, sustainable change. From treat meals to feng shui fridges, she offers eight life hacks to lower your carbon emissions while increasing your joy and fulfillment.
title: TED - How to feng shui your fridge — and other happy climate hacks; Jiaying Zhao

author: Chris
description: If we're going to solve the climate crisis, we need to talk about construction. The four main building materials that humans currently use -- concrete, steel, masonry and wood -- have a heavy environmental impact, but what if we had a fifth option? Architect Michael Green proposes an entirely new, natural medium inspired by the structure of trees and plants. Learn more about the carbon-sequestering solution to our construction conundrum that's laying the groundwork for a truly sustainable future.
title: TED - The natural building blocks of sustainable architecture; Michael Green

author: Chris
description: What does it mean to be an active citizen? It's about more than just voting and paying taxes, says social entrepreneur Gabriel Marmentini. He explains why we can't rely on the state alone to solve all our problems — and presents the four key ingredients for anyone to become a change-maker and engage in solving public issues.
title: TED - How to be an active citizen and spark change; Gabriel Marmentini

author: Chris
description: Over the last two decades, the wind power industry has grown at a dizzying pace. (Fun fact: a single rotation from one of the world's most powerful wind turbines can generate enough electricity to charge more than 1,400 cell phones.) Building off this exponential growth, Denmark's climate minister Dan Jørgensen lays out his plan to end the country's oil industry by 2050 and transition to a fossil-free future powered by wind energy.
title: TED - How wind energy could power Earth ... 18 times over; Dan Jørgensen

author: Chris
description: What shapes our perceptions (and misperceptions) about science? In an eye-opening talk, meteorologist J. Marshall Shepherd explains how confirmation bias, the Dunning-Kruger effect and cognitive dissonance impact what we think we know -- and shares ideas for how we can replace them with something much more powerful: knowledge.
title: TED - 3 kinds of bias that shape your worldview; J. Marshall Shepherd

author: Chris
description: Michael Shermer says the human tendency to believe strange things -- from alien abductions to dowsing rods -- boils down to two of the brain's most basic, hard-wired survival skills. He explains what they are, and how they get us into trouble.
title: TED - The pattern behind self-deception; Michael Shermer

author: Chris
description: Where do you draw the line between work and life? Writer Simone Stolzoff explores the problem with defining yourself by your job — and shows what it takes to reclaim your time and sense of meaning beyond the office.
title: TED - How to reclaim your life from work; Simone Stolzoff

author: Chris
description: What's the most important thing to look for when applying for a new job? Entrepreneur Marion Campan advocates for a focus on company culture above all else. She offers practical strategies for evaluating companies before accepting a new position — including how to ask the right questions about values, feedback and expectations — to help job seekers find positions where they can thrive.
title: TED - The secret to finding your ideal workplace; Marion Campan

author: Chris
description: What do you do when you're feeling stressed or anxious? Psychologist Andrew Miki explains how many of the coping mechanisms that help us feel better in the moment — like procrastinating, overusing our smartphones or endlessly scrolling social media — actually leave us feeling more depleted over time. He shows how you can break these habits in order to build up resilience and improve your self-confidence.
title: TED - Are your coping mechanisms healthy?; Andrew Miki

author: Chris
description: You know it's important to take care of your physical and mental health. But what about your social health? Social scientist Kasley Killam shows how feeling a sense of belonging and connection has concrete benefits to your overall health — and explains why it may be the missing key to living a longer and happier life.
title: TED - Why social health is key to happiness and longevity; Kasley Killam

author: Chris
description: What makes for a meaningful life? Social psychologist Brian S. Lowery explores three ideas tied to the experience of meaning and shows why simply pursuing personal achievements isn't the best way to find it.
title: TED - How to live a meaningful life; Brian S. Lowery

author: Chris
description: Stress. It makes your heart pound, your breathing quicken and your forehead sweat. But while stress has been made into a public health enemy, new research suggests that stress may only be bad for you if you believe that to be the case. Psychologist Kelly McGonigal urges us to see stress as a positive, and introduces us to an unsung mechanism for stress reduction: reaching out to others.
title: TED - How to make stress your friend; Kelly McGonigal

author: Chris
description: The happiest and healthiest people are those who have warm connections with others, says psychiatrist Robert Waldinger, who leads the Harvard Study of Adult Development — one of the longest-running studies of adult life ever conducted. Exploring the crucial link between social bonds and quality of life, he shares wisdom and insights into how to identify and strengthen the relationships that impact your well-being most. When it comes to the people in your inner circle, "Turn toward the voices that make you feel more open and more inclusive," he says.
title: TED - The secret to a happy life — lessons from 8 decades of research; Robert Waldinger

author: Chris
description: What makes you, you? Psychologists like to talk about our traits, or defined characteristics that make us who we are. But Brian Little is more interested in moments when we transcend those traits -- sometimes because our culture demands it of us, and sometimes because we demand it of ourselves. Join Little as he dissects the surprising differences between introverts and extroverts and explains why your personality may be more malleable than you think.
title: TED - Who are you, really? The puzzle of personality; Brian Little

author: Chris
description: When is the last time you did absolutely nothing for 10 whole minutes? Not texting, talking or even thinking? Mindfulness expert Andy Puddicombe describes the transformative power of doing just that: Refreshing your mind for 10 minutes a day, simply by being mindful and experiencing the present moment. (No need for incense or sitting in uncomfortable positions.)
title: TED - All it takes is 10 mindful minutes; Andy Puddicombe

author: Chris
description: Have you ever felt like you're talking, but nobody is listening? Here's Julian Treasure to help. In this useful talk, the sound expert demonstrates the how-to's of powerful speaking -- from some handy vocal exercises to tips on how to speak with empathy. A talk that might help the world sound more beautiful.
title: TED - How to speak so that people want to listen; Julian Treasure

author: Chris
description: Have you ever left a meeting thinking: everyone talked, but nothing was achieved? Chances are that people were listening to each other, just not in the same way. Listening experts Maegan Stephens and Nicole Lowenbraun unpack the four different ways to listen, sharing a practical framework that could change how you respond, build trust and get results — starting with just one simple question.
title: TED - How to be a great listener; Maegan Stephens and Nicole Lowenbraun

author: Chris
description: Everyone experiences loss, but how do you cope with the tough moments that follow? Resilience researcher Lucy Hone shares three hard-won strategies for developing the capacity to brave adversity, overcome struggle and face whatever may come head-on with fortitude and grace.
title: TED - 3 secrets of resilient people; Lucy Hone

author: Chris
description: César Hidalgo has a radical suggestion for fixing our broken political system: automate it! In this provocative talk, he outlines a bold idea to bypass politicians by empowering citizens to create personalized AI representatives that participate directly in democratic decisions. Explore a new way to make collective decisions and expand your understanding of democracy.
title: TED - A bold idea to replace politicians; César Hidalgo

author: Chris
description: It lurks within, emerging in conversation to share ineffective, premature suggestions … it's your advice monster, and we all have one, says writer and teacher Michael Bungay Stanier. He shares how giving advice can easily go astray, from solving the wrong problem to disempowering the very person you're trying to help, and offers a simple question to help you stay curious, strengthen your relationships — and tame that monster.
title: TED - How to tame your advice monster; Michael Bungay Stanier

author: Chris
description: When you stop comparing yourself to others, you can accomplish great things, says wheelchair athlete Dean Furness. He shares how, after losing the use of his legs in an accident, he discovered a powerful new mindset focused on redefining his "personal average" and getting better little by little.
title: TED - To overcome challenges, stop comparing yourself to others; Dean Furness

author: Chris
description: Perspective is everything, especially when it comes to examining your beliefs. Are you a soldier, prone to defending your viewpoint at all costs -- or a scout, spurred by curiosity? Julia Galef examines the motivations behind these two mindsets and how they shape the way we interpret information, interweaved with a compelling history lesson from 19th-century France. When your steadfast opinions are tested, Galef asks: "What do you most yearn for? Do you yearn to defend your own beliefs or do you yearn to see the world as clearly as you possibly can?"
title: TED - Why you think you're right -- even if you're wrong; Julia Galef

author: Chris
description: Can conflict actually bring you and your partner closer? It depends on how you fight, say Julie and John Gottman, the world's leading relationship scientists. They share why the way couples fight can predict the future of their relationships — and show how anybody can transform conflict into an opportunity for deeper connection and understanding.
title: TED - Even healthy couples fight — the difference is how; Julie and John Gottman

author: Chris
description: To spark action on climate change, the conventional wisdom says that awareness must precede action — but neuroscientist Kris De Meyer suggests the opposite is true: actions drive beliefs. He digs into the science behind decision-making and shows how you can rewire your brain to get unstuck on big challenges.
title: TED - Feeling stuck on climate change? Here's what to do; Kris De Meyer

author: Chris
description: You can't just "find" motivation, says scientist Ayelet Fishbach — you have to learn how to motivate yourself. She shares a handful of tips backed by 20 years of motivation research, offering surprisingly simple wisdom on how to optimize your goals, set yourself up for success and avoid the tempting calls of procrastination.
title: TED - How to set the right goals and stay motivated; Ayelet Fishbach

author: Chris
description: Our memories and bodies give us clues about who we are, but what happens when this guidance shifts? In this mind-bending talk, science writer Anil Ananthaswamy shares how the experiences of "altered selves" -- resulting from schizophrenia, Alzheimer's, foreign limb syndrome or other conditions -- shed light on the constructed nature of identity. He breaks down where our sense of self comes from and invites us to challenge our assumptions about who we are, with the aim of building a better you and a better world.
title: TED - Where does your sense of self come from? A scientific look; Anil Ananthaswamy

author: Chris
description: How do doctors in the emergency room stay calm and focused amidst the chaos? Drawing on years of experience, ER doctor Darria Long shares a straightforward framework to help you take back control and feel less overwhelmed when life starts to get "crazy busy."
title: TED - An ER doctor on triaging your "crazy busy" life; Darria Long

author: Chris
description: Chatbots might help you get work done faster — but at what cost? When we outsource our reasoning to artificial intelligence, we reduce ourselves to "middle managers for our own thoughts," says AI and design researcher Advait Sarkar. He examines the cognitive trade-offs of using AI at work and introduces a different kind of tool: one that encourages critical thinking, nudges reflection and actually helps you get smarter.
title: TED - How to stop AI from killing your critical thinking; Advait Sarkar

author: Chris
description: The United States is on track to win the AI race — and hollow itself out in the process, says Gina Raimondo, former Governor of Rhode Island and US Secretary of Commerce. In this unflinching look at the threat of AI-induced economic disruption and social unrest, she offers a concrete blueprint to prepare workers for what's coming next. "AI is a 100-year technology and needs a 100-year response," she says. Is America up to the challenge?
title: TED - A plan to stop AI from automating our decline; Gina Raimondo

author: Chris
description:
21 challenges facing modern humanity.

What must we do today to prepare for the world of tomorrow?

Will artificial intelligence replace humans? Can ecological catastrophe be avoided? What will a world of biotechnologically modified people look like? Will democracy survive? Will terrorists get their hands on nuclear weapons? Will the market decide everything?

Harari explains the modern world in an accessible way and outlines the prospects for its development. He seeks answers to the most pressing questions. He finds what unites all people, regardless of geography. He diagnoses problems, forecasts threats, but also the opportunities that the near future will bring us.
title: 21 Lessons for the 21st Century – Yuval Noah Harari

author: Chris
description: A completely new, sensational interpretation of events covering the first weeks of the German-Soviet war. Based on data found in previously classified materials and documents, as well as historical analysis and memoirs of war participants, the author debunks myths about the causes of the catastrophic defeats of the Red Army in the first months of the war. He emphasizes that the main reason for the Russian defeat
title: 22 June 1941, or How the Great Patriotic War Began – Mark Solonin

author: Chris
description:
Jay Shetty, author of the international bestseller "Think Like a Monk," returns with a revealing guide to all stages of a romantic relationship, combining lessons from ancient wisdom and modern knowledge.

Nobody taught us how to love. That is why, when in a relationship, we often rely primarily on what romantic movies and pop culture suggest. Now you can change that.

In his new book, Jay Shetty does not treat love as some ethereal concept, nor does he write about it using worn-out clichés. He presents concrete, easy-to-follow steps that will help you develop the ability to experience love fully and nurture it.
title: 8 Rules of Love – Jay Shetty

author: Chris
description:
A better life begins within you.

When you like yourself, reality takes on a whole new quality. You breathe more fully, smile more often, and approach everyday matters with greater ease. You stop living by others' expectations and start listening to yourself. More calm, energy, and joy in small things appear.

This change begins in your thoughts and emotions. They largely determine who you are and what daily life looks like. Positivity is not naivety or denial of difficult experiences – it is a conscious choice of attitude toward life. A choice that adds strength, courage, and inner lightness.
title: Jak żyć aby nie żałować. Pozytywność na codzień – Alina Adamowicz, Karolina Nowakowska

author: Chris
description:
If you don't know much about atomic energy – this book is for you.
If you know quite a lot – pick it up anyway, it's truly worth it.
If the atom frightens you – read it, because it will tame those fears.
If you oppose the development of nuclear energy – you must read it, because you will discover the arguments of those who believe this technology offers hope for halting climate change without deepening energy poverty across entire societies.
If you are a supporter of nuclear power – read it all the more, because it is a fascinating example of how to debate without bitterness, drawing on substantive arguments and with respect for those who think differently.
title: Atom dla klimatu – Urszula Kuczyńska

author: Chris
description:
An engrossing biography of one of the most outstanding politicians and versatile thinkers in history.

Benjamin Franklin was not only one of the Founding Fathers of the United States, but also a true Renaissance man who was ahead of his time in many respects. He was a brilliant scientist, inventor, entrepreneur, diplomat, writer, strategist, and one of the greatest political thinkers in history.

The personality of this effective politician and curious creator inspires today just as it did two centuries ago. His story teaches how to lead a life that is both practical and spiritual, how to achieve personal success while serving society.
title: Benjamin Franklin – Walter Isaacson

author: Chris
description:
The book is about rediscovering your own body, taking care of it, and learning to be aware of its existence. Contemplating the body makes us more focused on experiencing and feeling the present moment, allowing us to better understand our thoughts and feelings.
Practicing bodyfulness supports:
improved physical health – it strengthens the body, reduces pain and muscle tension, and improves breathing capacity. stress reduction – it suggests how to consciously understand our reactions to stressful situations and helps find optimal ways of coping with them. improved emotional wellbeing – it helps us better understand our emotions and feelings, which increases our psychological resilience.
title: Bodyfulness – Improving Your Relationship with Your Body Through the Senses, Breath, and Movement

author: Chris
description:
In "The God Delusion" Dawkins does not write (at least not directly) about biology. The subject of his book is religion and the relationship between science and faith. Dawkins, with the full force of his knowledge, talent and intellect, directly and straightforwardly rejects religion and all its claims (among others, and perhaps above all, the theists' delusion that religion is the source of morality).

He begins by exposing the false logical assumptions of religious beliefs, and then writes, among other things, about the evolutionary roots of theism.
title: The God Delusion – Richard Dawkins

author: Chris
description:
Rich Dad Poor Dad – about what the rich teach their children about money and what the poor and middle class do not know – has been at the top of the world's business bestseller lists for several years. The author, Robert Kiyosaki, opens our eyes to a world we will never learn about in school or at university. Modern education prepares children and young people for life in a world that no longer really exists.

Rich Dad Poor Dad is a handbook teaching a modern approach to making money.
title: Rich Dad, Poor Dad – Robert Kiyosaki

author: Chris
description:
You long for silence and rest, yet you feel your everyday life is becoming increasingly complicated? You get distracted easily, feel pressure and growing fatigue? It's becoming harder to maintain inner peace? If so, it's worth pausing for a moment and asking yourself what you can do to slow down and catch your breath despite your duties, difficult matters and worries.

Father Maximilien Le Fébure du Bus, a respected spiritual guide, will help you discover those areas of your daily life that need quieting and soothing. With his guidance, you will set out on a journey to explore the simplicity of life and experience true joy in each day.
title: Return to Simplicity. How to Calm the Spirit in a Busy World – Maximilien Le Fébure du Bus

author: Chris
description:
Atomic Habits is a simple, proven method for building good habits and breaking bad ones.

The foundation of the book is a habit model consisting of four steps (cue, craving, response, and reward) and four laws of behavior change that follow from these steps.

The assumptions I present form an integrated model based on cognitive and behavioral sciences. In my opinion, it is one of the first models of human behavior that accounts for the influence of both external stimuli and internal emotions on habits.
title: Atomic Habits – James Clear

author: Chris
description:
A groundbreaking, timeless bestseller in an exclusive edition.
This book is worth having at home and worth returning to.

Millions of readers, including global business and political leaders, continually refer to How to Win Friends and Influence People. This is the best proof that the lessons taught by Dale Carnegie, which launched the self-development movement, have stood the test of time and gained a universal character. These are classic principles of conduct in the best sense of the word, and the book's general premises remain relevant for successive generations.
title: How to Win Friends and Influence People – Dale Carnegie

author: Chris
description:
Initiates positive changes in the mind, community or organization. Actively works on solving problems, trying to make a significant impact and improve the lives of others. Has a strong sense of purpose that drives meaningful action. Who is this? The titular Changemaker!

Written by Alex Budak, a distinguished scholar from the University of California, in the form of an accessible guide, it calls to action by showing how changing from where you are can transform your career, community, and even the world.
title: Becoming a Changemaker: An Actionable, Inclusive Guide to Leading Positive Change at Any Level – Alex Budak

author: Chris
description:
Everyone has read a product label at least once in their life. The ingredients list of seemingly simple food products can make for particularly interesting reading.

How do you decode the abbreviations found there, and which ones deserve special attention? The answers come from the bestselling author of *Don't Eat That!* and *Sugar Mafia*, whose publications are a nightmare for food corporations.

As Dr. Grimm argues in his latest book, food produced on an industrial scale needs chemical additives. Unfortunately, humans do not — these additives are simply harmful to us.
title: Chemistry in Food – Hans-Ulrich Grimm

author: Chris
description: What makes some liquids solidify while others don't? How is it possible that some insects can walk on water? Is the taste of wine correlated with its color? How do ordinary waves form, and how do tsunamis? When was the first glue invented? Mark Miodownik, materials scientist and unrivaled science communicator, takes us on a journey through the world of wonderful substances.
title: Liquid: The Delightful and Dangerous Substances That Flow Through Our Lives – Mark Miodownik

author: Chris
description: We don't usually think about the significance and impact of genetics on our lives. It seems like a complicated and rather distant field of knowledge. However, it turns out that we encounter it every day. Genetically modified food, stem cells used in medicine and cosmetics, vaccinations and gene therapies – these are just some examples. Genetics is one of the fastest-growing fields of science, entering our lives with momentum. Scientific achievements in this field are most often applied in medicine and health promotion.
title: What Hides in Our Genes? The Greatest Puzzle of Humanity – Ewa Bartnik

author: Chris
description: The book by Michael Yardney and Tom Corley is a chance to learn the specific habits of wealthy people that you need to adopt in order to succeed. It is also an opportunity to discover the habits of the poor, which are worth knowing so you can break free from them. The authors spent five years studying and analyzing the daily practices of 233 successful people and 128 who did not succeed. In the book, they reveal all the differences between the habits of both groups studied. And there are truly many of them.
title: Rich Habits Poor Habits – Tom Corley, Michael Yardney

author: Chris
description:
A therapy guru reveals what shapes us, why it matters, and offers practical ways to live a happier life.

Do you know how your childhood affects your self-perception and relationships with others? How school, being a victim of bullying, gender expectations, advertising, and even the media you encounter daily impact your wellbeing? Do you want to learn what emotions really are, where they come from, and how to cope with them when you fear they will overwhelm you?

Clinical psychologist Sophie Mort, known online as Dr. Soph, will help you sort through difficult emotions and tackle false beliefs about yourself.
title: A Manual of Being Human – Sophie Mort

author: Chris
description:
Life is all around us, rich and diverse. It truly is a miracle. But what does it actually mean to be alive, and how do we decide what is life and what is not?

After a lifetime dedicated to science, Nobel laureate Sir Paul Nurse, one of the world's leading scientists, took on the challenge of defining what life is. The result is this guide, written with great insight, wit and grace, which takes readers on a journey through the five pillars of biology – the cell, the gene, evolution by natural selection, life as chemistry and life as information – and shows how biology has transformed itself and how it is changing the world, while revealing where modern research is headed.
title: What is Life? Understand Biology in Five Steps – Paul Nurse

author: Chris
description:
Does your child often ignore established rules, put off responsibilities "for later," or respond reluctantly to your requests? Or perhaps daily conflicts around studying, tidying up, or screen time are starting to overwhelm you? Paul Dix, a renowned expert in children's behaviour, shows how to improve family relationships by introducing a culture of calm, consistency, and understanding into the home.

Most importantly, he emphasizes that real change begins with the parents — with their behaviour, attitude, and approach.

In this book you will find:

Simple strategies for difficult situations: You will learn how to stay calm when a child erupts emotionally or refuses to cooperate.
title: When the Parents Change, Everything Changes. Seismic Shifts in Children's Behaviour – Paul Dix

author: Chris
description:
Where do good ideas come from? Is there a way to have more of them? And why do they often arrive at strange moments?

To answer these questions, the author – like Alice following the White Rabbit to Wonderland – searches for the sources of creativity. She talks with neurologists, scientists, writers, musicians, comedians, artists and philosophers, lets current pass through her frontal lobe, signs up for improvisation and yoga nidra classes, visits a flotation tank, gets bored, celebrates purposelessness, daydreams, and learns to silence her inner critic – her own Queen of Hearts.
title: Creativity – Hilde Østby

author: Chris
description:
Why are some nations rich and others poor? Why are they so divided by wealth and poverty, health and disease, plenty and hunger?

The brilliant and enormously inspiring book by Acemoglu and Robinson, world experts on development issues, calls for shedding illusions. Countries grow when they build political and economic institutions conducive to development, and they fail — often in spectacular fashion — when those institutions ossify or cease to function. The nation then sinks into stagnation and decline.
title: Why Nations Fail – Daron Acemoglu, James A. Robinson

author: Chris
description:
An eye-opening, groundbreaking tour of the goals and reasons for work in our lives, showing how work functions in our culture and how one can find their own path to happiness in the workplace.

Why do we work? The question seems so simple. But Professor Barry Schwartz argues that the answer is surprising and complex.

We have long been taught that the main reason we work is money. We have even shaped the infrastructure of our society to reflect this belief. Why, then, are so many people dissatisfied with their jobs, despite the wages they receive?
title: Why We Work – Barry Schwartz

author: Chris
description:
Dr James Goodwin, a professor of physiology, argues that mental condition depends largely not on genetic factors, but on our behaviors: diet, physical activity, sleep hygiene, stress exposure, frequency and quality of social contacts, and the ability to experience happiness.

He presents innovative methods of brain stimulation, including regenerative medicine, drawing on various medical fields such as dietetics, microbiology, and psychology, as well as the latest scientific research. The book contains a range of practical tips and a brain training program that can be done at home.
title: Supercharge Your Brain – James Goodwin

author: Chris
description: Drive is an exceptional book that fertilizes thinking and drives effective action. Pink puts forward strong arguments to rethink motivation and provides the tools needed to make changes in one's own life.
title: Drive. The Surprising Truth About What Motivates Us – Daniel H. Pink

author: Chris
description:
Do you feel your potential is trapped in the grey everyday routine? Do you want to finally awaken your best self? Do you believe everyone can aim high and achieve above-average results in both private and professional life?

The lessons in this guide will help transform your life by:
● discovering the personal practices of successful people,
● gaining valuable experience from those who have mastered the tools for achieving a magical work-life balance,
● taking on the challenge of becoming a better version of yourself,
● developing skills that will help change your life.
title: The Greatness Guide: 101 Lessons for Making What's Good at Work and in Life Even Better – Robin Sharma

author: Chris
description: "The Strange Order of Things" is a groundbreaking book dedicated to homeostasis; this state regulates human physiological processes in a range that enables not only survival but also flourishing. Damasio explains that biologically, psychologically, and even socially we descend from a long line beginning with single living cells; that our minds and cultures are connected by an invisible thread to archaic single-celled organisms and other primitive life forms; and finally, that within our very chemistry lies a powerful force, a drive to sustain life in all its manifestations, including the development of genes that help regulate and transmit it.
title: The Strange Order of Things: Life, Feeling, and the Making of Cultures – Antonio Damasio

author: Chris
description:
Einstein – an icon of our times. His wild hair, bright eyes, charming and warm personality, and extraordinary mind have made his face a symbol and his name a synonym for genius.

A rebel from childhood, a free spirit who never stopped asking questions. He questioned what others took for granted and saw challenging strangeness in the simplest phenomena. Einstein's character, creativity, and imagination intertwined to shape his life and scientific work, the fruits of which forever changed our understanding of time, space, and the nature of reality.

Walter Isaacson – author of bestselling biographies, including
title: Einstein. His Life and Universe – Walter Isaacson

author: Chris
description:
This is not a book about the "economics of food," nor a book pairing economics with cuisine. It is a book about globalization, climate change, migration, scarcity, automation, and many other important topics, presented in an easily digestible form.

Ha-Joon Chang cleverly and entertainingly weaves stories about cooking and food together with economics, making ambitious economic ideas not only palatable but even delicious.
title: Edible Economics: A Hungry Economist Explains the World – Ha-Joon Chang

author: Chris
description:
A new biography from the bestselling author of "Steve Jobs," "Leonardo da Vinci," "The Innovators," and "The Code Breaker"!

"Elon Musk" is a remarkably intimate story of the most fascinating and controversial innovator of our time — a rule-breaking visionary who helped usher the world into the era of electric vehicles, private space exploration, and artificial intelligence. Oh, and he took over Twitter.

Elon Musk spent his childhood in South Africa. It was not an easy one. He was frequently a target of his peers. One day, a group of boys pushed him down concrete stairs and kicked him mercilessly, horribly battering his face. He spent a week in the hospital.
title: Elon Musk – Walter Isaacson

author: Chris
description: On an exceptionally dark and sweltering Caribbean night, Brendon Burchard stood bloodied on the crumpled hood of his wrecked car. It was then he understood that, like each of us, he is an ordinary mortal, and that at the end of life every person will seek answers to a few basic questions: "Did I truly live? Did I love and give of myself to others? Did I accomplish something meaningful and significant in my life?"
title: The Charge: Activating The 10 Human Drives That Make You Feel Alive – Brendon Burchard

author: Chris
description:
To therapists' offices come people who are lonely, helpless in being alone with themselves. Those who experience existential pain and find no one with whom they could share that pain or who could relieve it. But loneliness is not the same as being alone.
Prof. Bogdan de Barbaro

How is it that in a world where we have so many social contacts, loneliness is not only a global problem, but also a cause of many illnesses, including depression?

Does the culture of "I" generate loneliness? Can focusing only on oneself, neglecting the values of community, lead to loneliness? When is solitude necessary, and how does it differ from the feeling of loneliness?
title: The Epidemic of Loneliness. How to Build Lasting Bonds in the Modern World – Agnieszka Łopatowska, Monika Szubrycht

author: Chris
description:
How many girls complete primary school in low-income countries? What is the current average life expectancy? How many children will there be in the world in 2100? These are the questions that Hans Rosling, Swedish professor of public health and director of the Gapminder Foundation, poses to the reader at the start of this fascinating book.

The author demonstrates that most educated people — even prominent scientists and high-ranking politicians — give the wrong answers to these questions.
title: Factfulness: Ten Reasons We're Wrong About the World - and Why Things Are Better Than You Think – Hans Rosling

author: Chris
description:
What is equal is not always fair. What is fair is not always equal. Discover an innovative way to divide household duties to gain more time and more mindful relationships.

Do you feel like you're the parent responsible for everything? You make sure the kids do their homework, the fridge isn't empty, the bills are paid on time – and much more. Does it feel unfair? You're right. It's time to change that.

A new way of organizing family life
Eve Rodsky interviewed over five hundred people to understand what household work involves, how demanding it is, and how it can be done more efficiently and effectively.
title: Fair Play: A Game-Changing Solution For When You Have Too Much To Do (And More Life to Live) – Eve Rodsky

author: Chris
description:
The story seems familiar, yet has never been told in full. The relationship between Hollywood's most desired star and America's most charismatic president lasted ten years before transforming into a love story under the strict surveillance of the media and state agencies. Recorded by the mafia, wiretapped by the KGB, followed by the CIA, the lovers were never alone.

François Forestier's account — journalist, novelist and biographer for Le Nouvel Observateur — is impeccably researched and brilliantly written, painting an original and mad portrait of a repulsive America where great political puppets, gangsters and billionaires wage a merciless war against one another.
title: Marilyn and JFK – François Forestier

author: Chris
description: M.K. Gandhi is one of the most inspiring figures of the twentieth century, a proponent of pacifism as a means of political struggle and one of the founding fathers of modern Indian statehood. This is a classic autobiography that tells, in Gandhi's own words, the story of his life and how he developed his concept of nonviolence and passive resistance, which paved the way for India's independence and became the foundation of many liberation movements.
title: Gandhi: An Autobiography – Gandhi M.K.

author: Chris
description:
We share 51% of our genes with yeast and 98% with chimpanzees, so it is not genetics that makes us human.

Dr Euan Ashley, Stanford professor of medicine, tells the story of breakthrough advances in precision medicine. It is a true diagnostic journey of patients and an account of the hard work of doctors and scientists.

Since the Human Genome Project was completed in 2003, the cost of genome sequencing has been falling at a staggering pace — as if the price of a Ferrari had dropped from 350,000 dollars to just 40 cents.
title: The Genome Odyssey: Medical Mysteries and the Incredible Quest to Solve Them – Euan Angus Ashley

author: Chris
description:
A work by one of the leading historians presents a striking correlation between the upheavals that shook the entire world in the mid-17th century and the weather changes that occurred at the same time. The question inevitably arises: are we prepared to deal with the effects of climate change in our own times?

"Based on impressive research, written in vivid language, and intellectually captivating... It is not only shocking and convincing, but stands as a monument to scholarly dedication... I hope its reading will spark debate for decades to come."
title: Global Crisis: War, Climate Change and Catastrophe in the Seventeenth Century – Geoffrey Parker

author: Chris
description:
An international bestseller translated into over forty languages.

Up to ninety percent of us experience sudden glucose spikes — and have no idea. The symptoms? Food cravings, constant fatigue, brain fog, sleep problems, weakened immunity, acne… And over time, chronic diseases such as type 2 diabetes, cancer, or dementia.

The author of Glucose Revolution presents groundbreaking scientific discoveries in an accessible way and shows how to take care of your health without making radical changes.
title: Glucose Revolution: The Life-Changing Power of Balancing Your Blood Sugar – Jessie Inchauspé

author: Chris
description:
When we talk about hormones, we often think of them as a "women's problem." Yet our hormones regulate everything from sleep and nutrition to mood and stress responses. In this guide, Davinia Taylor, entrepreneur and biohacking pioneer, describes how to best optimize all our hormones.

The author offers medically backed advice on how diet and supplements (hacks) can balance our cortisol, adrenaline, dopamine and more, even vitamin D (yes, it's a hormone). And the solutions may be within reach — in your kitchen cupboards.
title: Hack Your Hormones: Effortless Weight Loss. Better Focus. Deeper Sleep. More Energy – Davinia Taylor

author: Chris
description: Henryk Sienkiewicz is certainly among the most widely read and best known Polish writers in the world. It is no exaggeration to say that his works shaped the imagination of several generations of Poles. Quo Vadis, a novel deserving the title of all-time bestseller and translated into 50 languages, is the only work of Polish literature included in the canon of world literature.
title: Henryk Sienkiewicz: Dandy and Celebrity – Iwona Kienzler

author: Chris
description:
If crows practiced farming, how would they do it? How did great domesticated horses evolve from tiny horses frolicking in prehistoric heat? Why do we become more brutal as the temperature rises?

The answers to these questions became the starting point for writing a one-of-a-kind history of the future, in two scenarios: with humans and without them. Which is more realistic? Our actions will decide. To survive, we must use our vast knowledge of other species to understand the laws of nature and live in harmony with them.
title: A Natural History of the Future – Rob Dunn

author: Chris
description: The book that revolutionized thinking about health and showed that the gut, one of our most important organs, has an irresistible charm and can be discussed in a clear, vivid, and wonderfully witty way. Read the book that millions of people around the world have gone crazy about, and your perception of your own body will change by 180 degrees. Giulia Enders can like no one else talk about what happens in our gut and how the processes there translate into various, often surprising, aspects of our lives, while her fresh perspective is complemented by hilarious drawings by her sister Jill. Immunity, body weight, susceptibility to allergies, energy levels?
title: Gut: The Inside Story of Our Body's Most Underrated Organ – Giulia Enders

author: Chris
description:
Can we hope that our changeable nature, sometimes fleeting or trivial aspirations, behaviors, and ultimately spirituality, can be explained through knowledge of biological mechanisms?

Neurobiologist Pier Vincenzo Piazza believes that modern biology can explain not only how processes in the human body occur, but also why things happen in our inner world.

Why do we seek freedom, yet also love order?

What makes us consider ourselves the dominant species on Earth, and are we truly superior to other animals?
title: Homo biologicus: How Biology Explains Human Nature – Pier Vincenzo Piazza

author: Chris
description:
Where will the pursuit of immortality lead us?

One of the most important books in recent years.

The aging body is now merely a technical problem. Soon the wealthiest will be able to repair it effectively. What will the world look like if humans become immortal? What use will religions and philosophies be then? Will artificial intelligence permanently replace the human mind? As we gradually alter our minds, will a new species quietly emerge — a god-man, homo deus?

Harari is a visionary storyteller who grounds his reflections on the direction of civilization in deep analysis of the past and in what is most pressing — here and now.
title: Homo Deus: A Brief History of Tomorrow – Yuval Noah Harari

author: Chris
description:
In 2011, the acclaimed biography of Apple founder Steve Jobs became an international bestseller and one of the best-selling biographies of all time. Its author, Walter Isaacson, in his latest book writes about the people to whom we owe the arrival and flourishing of the information age and the digital world. The Innovators is a fascinating story, spanning over a century and a half, about how innovation happens and how collaboration and cooperation unleash creativity, leading to revolutionary changes in our daily lives.

*** After the bestselling biography of Steve Jobs, Walter Isaacson presents his next book.
title: The Innovators: How a Group of Hackers, Geniuses and Geeks Created the Digital Revolution – Walter Isaacson

author: Chris
description: Emotional intelligence is not an innate trait. The book shows when and by what methods it can be developed in children, in order to ensure they make the best possible use of their innate abilities in achieving success in life.
title: Emotional Intelligence – Daniel Goleman

author: Chris
description: During his over thirty years of work as a sex therapist and marriage counselor with individuals and couples, Dr. Marty Klein consistently observes that although most people claim they desire pleasure and closeness in their sex lives, that is not what they actually focus on. Instead, we become consumed by how we look, what our partner thinks of us, whether we are performing well, and whether we are normal. Instead of experiencing, we think, worry, and judge. Sex with these qualities cannot be exciting, cannot provide a sense of intimacy, nor can it be our expression of sexuality.
title: Sexual Intelligence. What We Really Want from Sex - and How to Get It – Marty Klein

author: Chris
description:
Award-winning journalist Stephen L. Petranek claims that by 2027 people will be living on Mars. He argues that life on Mars is not only possible, but inevitable.

It sounds like science fiction, but Stephen L. Petranek considers it a fact: within twenty years, people will be living on Mars. They will have to. In this provocative book, which combines business, science, and human experience, Petranek maintains that life on Mars is an essential backup plan for humanity, and explains in fascinating detail how it will happen.

The race is already underway.
title: How We'll Live on Mars – Stephen Petranek

author: Chris
description:
A perverse and captivating guide on how… to live decently.

The co-creator of "The Good Place," "Parks and Recreation," and the American version of "The Office" draws freely from two and a half thousand years of philosophical thought to create a light, funny, and at the same time thoroughly serious book about ethics — without pretension, tedium, or academic dryness.

Most of us think of ourselves as good people. But can we always flawlessly determine what is right and what is wrong? Especially in the modern world, where at every turn we face difficult decisions, not-so-wise advice, and other traps?
title: How to Be Perfect: The Correct Answer to Every Moral Question – Michael Schur

author: Chris
description: How can we greet each morning with greater optimism and hope for the future? How can we consciously become happier? The paradox of happiness is that the more we value it, the more we desire it, the more elusive it becomes. Psychologist Tal Ben-Shahar presents his original method (SPIRE) for finding one's own happiness. He argues that by breaking happiness down into five key elements and working to achieve them, we set ourselves on the path to a happy life.
title: Happier, no matter what. – Tal Ben-Shahar

author: Chris
description:
Royal Society Prize 2020 for Best Popular Science Book

Dr Camilla Pang was diagnosed at age eight with autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, and generalized anxiety disorder. She didn't understand most human behaviors or emotions, and couldn't pick up on social cues. She felt as though no one had given her an instruction manual for being human.
Now, armed with a PhD in biochemistry, Dr Camilla Pang tackles our ambiguous social customs and identifies what it truly means to be human.
What can proteins, machine learning, and molecular chemistry teach us about the complexity of human behavior and the world around us?
title: Explaining Humans: What Science Can Teach Us about Life, Love and Relationships – Camilla Pang

author: Chris
description:
In this remarkable book, Steven Pinker, one of the world's leading thinkers, clearly and with humor explains what the mind is, how it evolved, and how it allows us to see, think, feel, enjoy art, and ponder the mysteries of life.

What makes us rational – and why are we so often irrational? How do we see in three dimensions? What makes us happy, frightened, angry, disgusted, or sexually aroused? Why do we fall in love? And how do we wrestle with the puzzles of morality, religion, and consciousness?
title: How the Mind Works – Steven Pinker

author: Chris
description:
Relationships build or ruin our lives.

Eric Barker thoroughly examined conventional wisdom about human relationships, weaving astonishing scientific facts into a compelling narrative. All to help you build better friendships, rekindle feelings, and create satisfying bonds with everyone in your life. It is a humorous guide to the art of building better relationships, a remedy for some of the greatest ailments of our time – growing emotional distance and loneliness.

However, the author states bluntly: "You will hate me […]
title: Plays well with others. The Surprising Science Behind Why Everything You Know About Relationships is (Mostly) Wrong – Eric Barker

author: Chris
description:
Do you worry about things beyond your control? Do you dwell on past events or constantly anticipate what might go wrong? Worrying can rob you of peace, energy, and joy in everyday life.

In his timeless guide, Dale Carnegie shows how to break the cycle of anxiety and look at problems from a new perspective. He advises how to handle difficult situations, make decisions, free yourself from unnecessary fears, and focus on what you can actually influence.
title: How to Stop Worrying and Start Living – Dale Carnegie

author: Chris
description: Emotions are talked about frequently and at length. Most people have difficulty recognizing and regulating their emotions. They feel overwhelmed and flooded by feelings, or conversely, claim to feel nothing at all.
title: How to Understand, Name and Regulate Your Emotions – Olga Daliga

author: Chris
description:
The first book this accessible to show how each of us can save the world.

Not long ago, Areta Szpura was making waves in the fashion industry. Clothes from the "Local Heroes" brand, of which she is a co-founder, were worn by Rihanna, Miley Cyrus, Ellie Goulding, Kylie Jenner and Justin Bieber. Yet her string of successes didn't diminish her sensitivity to how unecological the fashion world is. Horrified by the enormous amounts of waste produced by the textile industry, Areta left her thriving brand to focus on saving the planet. She, together with the Noizz editorial team, launched the "No Straw Here" campaign. But cutting out straws alone isn't enough — it's time for big changes!
title: How to Save the World? What Good Can You Do for the Planet – Areta Szpura

author: Chris
description: This book does not yet have a description. Add a description +
title: How to Raise a Happy and Mentally Resilient Child. A Guide for Parents of Children of All Ages – Beth Mosley

author: Chris
description: "A Brief History of Time," Stephen Hawking's global bestseller, has entered the canon of popular science literature. The book's success was due both to the author's renown and to the topics it covers: the nature of the cosmos, the role of God in creation, and the history and future of the universe. Readers repeatedly pointed out to Hawking the difficulties in understanding some of the most important concepts discussed in his book. Such were the reasons behind the creation of A Briefer History of Time — the author's desire to make its content more accessible to readers, as well as to supplement it with the latest observations and scientific discoveries.
title: A Briefer History of Time – Stephen Hawking, Leonard Mlodinow

author: Chris
description:
What future awaits Europe's largest economy?

Until recently, Germany appeared to be a model of economic and political success. It seemed that the export-driven German economic model guaranteed prosperity and well-being, and that Angela Merkel was the "true leader of the free world." However, the geopolitical changes of recent years have shown that Germany must pay a high price for its long-standing dependence on cheap Russian gas and its inability to keep pace with American and Chinese automotive companies in the race toward electromobility.
title: Kaput: The End of the German Miracle – Wolfgang Münchau

author: Chris
description:
Do you feel that mental health support is out of your reach? Maybe you've tried therapy but haven't found a therapist you feel comfortable with? Or perhaps you simply want to take care of your mental health on your own? This book is just for you!

Liz Kelly, an experienced therapist, will guide you through the complexities of mental health in a simple, accessible way and — most importantly — with a touch of humor. Whether you're a newcomer to the world of self-development or have therapy sessions behind you, this book offers concrete tools to help you better cope with everyday challenges.
title: It's Not Always Depression – Liz Kelly

author: Chris
description:
Can you literally die of loneliness? Is there a connection between the ability to express emotions and Alzheimer's disease? Can a "cancer personality" be defined?

Drawing on in-depth scientific research, Dr. Gabor Maté answers questions about the mind-body connection. He presents scientific evidence for the role that stress and emotions play in the occurrence of a range of common diseases such as arthritis, cancer, diabetes, heart disease, irritable bowel syndrome, and multiple sclerosis.
title: When The Body Says No: The Cost of Hidden Stress – Gabor Maté

author: Chris
description:
Bolesław Prus – an orphan without a home, a sixteen-year-old insurgent balancing on the edge of life and death, a mathematics fanatic who despised novels yet wrote "The Doll." A moralist and a rebel. A myth, and at the same time a man of flesh and blood.

The biography by Iwona Kienzler strips Aleksander Głowacki (the real name of Bolesław Prus) of scholarly pathos and monumental solemnity. It presents him as a man entangled in passions and romances, a man who was ill, attacked by critics, and struggling with his own fears until the end of his life.
title: Prus. The Hidden Life of a Writer – Iwona Kienzler

author: Chris
description:
Best Book of 2019 — "Financial Times" and "The Guardian"

Some people reject the fact that our planet is warming due to human activity. But do those of us who accept the reality of the man-made climate catastrophe truly believe in it? If we really believed it, we would surely choose to act in accordance with what we know. And yet we hardly act at all.

In We Are the Weather, Jonathan Safran Foer explores the fundamental dilemma of our times in a surprising and deeply personal way. The task of saving the planet requires a great reckoning with our own.
title: We Are the Weather: Saving the Planet Begins at Breakfast – Jonathan Safran Foer

author: Chris
description:
A new excellent book by an outstanding biographer, author of the bestsellers Steve Jobs and Leonardo da Vinci. A captivating story about Nobel laureate Jennifer Doudna and other remarkable scientists who uncover incredible secrets of nature and life to push humanity's development even further. Plot twists, emotions, rivalry between research groups, and important questions on the borders of philosophy, ethics, and morality.

One day, sixth-grader Jennifer Doudna came home from school to find that her father had left a book on her bed: "The Double Helix." She was pleased, thinking it was one of those thrillers she loved so much.
title: The Code Breaker: Jennifer Doudna, Gene Editing, and the Future of the Human Race – Walter Isaacson

author: Chris
description:
An ever-growing percentage of the world's population suffers from obesity and related diseases. The multi-billion-dollar diet industry constantly offers new, trendy diets and ineffective long-term solutions — all at the cost of your health. As a result, you remain trapped in a vicious cycle of food addiction, toxic hunger, and overeating.

In Eat to Live, Dr. Joel Fuhrman demonstrates how to break free from this trap once and for all. He provides readers with invaluable nutritional guidance and shows how proper eating can lead to a healthier and happier life.
title: The End of Dieting: How to Live for Life – Joel Fuhrman

author: Chris
description:
"Cosmos: Possible Worlds" is the next installment of the captivating stellar odyssey begun by Carl Sagan and Ann Druyan. The Cosmos series became a global phenomenon, broadcast in 181 countries worldwide. In this part, Ann Druyan continues the electrifying journey through 14 billion years of cosmic evolution, unveiling nature's deepest secrets.

Druyan describes our fate from the emergence of life on Earth in the ocean's depths around four billion years ago, to a future when spacecraft venture into other parts of the galaxy, their multigenerational crews exploring worlds still unknown to us. It is a story of ideas that shaped the development of science.
title: Cosmos: Possible Worlds – Ann Druyan

author: Chris
description:
A real man is an endangered species. This book is a cry for help for gentlemen.

Modern men increasingly fail to match the cultural image that requires them to be a woman's pillar of support, a symbol of security and the fight for survival. Men today are often weak, tired, overworked, with diminished sexual needs.
It is becoming harder to find in them the traits that distinguish the male from the female. The world is also becoming populated by metrosexual individuals, who are essentially men, yet far more resembling genderless creatures.
title: A Book Only for Men – Ewa Kempisty-Jeznach

author: Chris
description:
Discover how to live more peacefully in an increasingly restless world.

Anxiety is an emotion that most people wrongly judge as negative. We treat it like an enemy in our mind, when in reality anxiety is our inner hero. It always tries to protect us from threats, but sometimes misjudges the dangers lurking in the modern world. This book is intended for people struggling with anxiety, intrusive thoughts, and panic attacks. It offers a gentle, compassionate approach to the problem.
title: Anxiety. How to Defeat the Monster – Eric Goodman

author: Chris
description: To discover what physics truly is, one must take risks and stop fearing even the most seemingly outlandish ideas. In "Fear of a Black Universe," Stephon Alexander argues that great theories always emerge outside the mainstream, born of intuition and improvisation. Following this path, he tackles the greatest challenges of modern physics — from the question of what existed before the Big Bang, through dark matter and energy, to contemplating the nature of consciousness.
title: Fear of a Black Universe: An Outsider's Guide to the Future of Physics – Stephon Alexander

author: Chris
description: The author of acclaimed bestsellers such as Steve Jobs, Einstein, Benjamin Franklin, and The Innovators presents his new book – a fascinating biography of Leonardo da Vinci. Drawing on thousands of pages of Leonardo's notes and the latest discoveries about the genius's life and work, Walter Isaacson weaves a compelling narrative that masterfully intertwines Leonardo's artistic creativity with his scientific achievements. Leonardo's brush produced two of the most famous paintings in the history of art: The Last Supper and the Mona Lisa. Yet he saw himself not only as a painter, but also as a scientist and engineer.
title: Leonardo da Vinci – Walter Isaacson

author: Chris
description: Some problems are hard to solve, costly, and fixing them helps little. Others we know how to solve at low cost and with great effect. We should first focus on sensible things. Governments and philanthropists should concentrate on these 12 most sensible steps: eliminate tuberculosis, malaria, and chronic diseases, fight malnutrition, improve education, increase trade, implement e-procurement, and secure land ownership. This will greatly improve the world's situation. The cost is 35 billion dollars per year. The benefits include saving 4.2 million human lives each year and generating 1.1 trillion dollars more for the world's poor.
title: Best Things First – Bjorn Lomborg

author: Chris
description:
"Magellan" by Stefan Zweig is a literary biography combining solid historical facts with the craft and flowing style of belles-lettres.
Zweig describes the life and great expedition of Ferdinand Magellan through the lens of the protagonist's psychology, giving the facts a narrative and emotional character of a novel, while remaining faithful to the historical truth of the first circumnavigation of the Earth.
The writer focuses on the Portuguese navigator's determination in the face of mutiny, hunger and disease. The author emphasizes the triumph of human will and the tragic price of genius, presenting the discovery of the strait and the circumnavigation as a unification of the world.
title: Magellan – Stefan Zweig

author: Chris
description: Marriage is for adults, but very few of us enter into matrimony as mature people. Maturity takes time and is difficult, and for some — unattainable. Yet marriage, though it can be the most irritating of human relationships, can also serve as a driver of our growth. By coming to terms, in one way or another, with the disappointments, demands, and surprising complexities of everyday married life, we can create — and there is no contradiction here — a mature marriage.
title: Marriage for the Advanced, or Everything We Would Like and Should Know to Enjoy a Successful Relationship – Judith Viorst

author: Chris
description:
Being an essentialist is not about doing more in less time, but about doing only the right things. Have you ever felt like you were spreading yourself too thin? Do you feel overworked and at the same time of little use? Do you often feel busy but not productive? Do you feel as if other people are constantly stealing your time?

If you answered yes to any of the above questions, the path of essentialism will lead you to freedom. Essentialism is more than a time management strategy or a productivity technique.
title: Essentialism. The Disciplined Pursuit of Less – Greg McKeown

author: Chris
description:
The author of the worldwide bestseller Essentialism presents an inspiring guide to achieving goals and shows how we can make it easier to do the right things. It all starts with a simple principle: WHAT MATTERS MOST DOESN'T HAVE TO BE HARD.

Do you ever feel like:
• you're running faster and faster, but not getting closer to your goals?
• you want to give more of yourself, but you lack the energy?
• you're on the edge of burnout?
• everything is much harder than it should be?

People familiar with such feelings are usually disciplined and focused. Engaged and motivated. Yet they are also utterly exhausted.
title: Effortless: Make It Easier to Do What Matters Most – Greg McKeown

author: Chris
description:
If he lived today, he would probably be a celebrity gossip portal or tabloid hero. His relationships with women would cause a sensation. He had affairs with married women, and when he finally started a family, he lived in a love triangle — or, according to some, even a quadrangle. Media attention might also have been brought by his membership in the Towianists or his controversial views, especially since he used a university lectern to proclaim them. It is no wonder that although Mickiewicz was hailed as a national bard, the poet stirred emotions and provoked disputes even among his contemporaries.
What did young Adam take with him on his journey to Vilnius?
title: Mickiewicz. Loves and Affairs – Iwona Kienzler

author: Chris
description:
The book's promise is simple: if you buy it on Friday, by Monday you'll be better at your job.
The guide is based on an easy-to-master principle: every big goal, healthy habit, complex task, and even what we consider character traits can be broken down into small, manageable skills.

The book contains a collection of information and effective solutions worth knowing at every stage of your career and life. It is designed to deliver benefits quickly – you don't have to wait until the last page to feel its impact on your daily functioning and work organization.
title: Microskills: Small Actions, Big Impact – Adaira Landry, Resa E. Lewiss

author: Chris
description:
Do you often feel that others handle daily life better than you? Do you find it easy to list your flaws, but struggle to name your strengths?

Self-esteem and a positive self-image can — and should! — be shaped at every stage of life, in order to maintain mental balance and… like yourself as you would a good friend. It is simpler than it might seem — all you need is a guide.
title: Fall in Love with Yourself – Walter Riso

author: Chris
description: This is not a book about inevitable doom. It is a book about hope. Drawing on knowledge from various fields – history, economics, anthropology, philosophy and the sciences – Jason Hickel offers a brilliant analysis of capitalism (with a refreshing perspective on its history) and proposes a vision of alternative development, breaking with the madness of perpetual growth. He writes about how to move from an economy organized around domination and exploitation to one based on global justice and mutual exchange of benefits with the natural world. He exposes the weaknesses of fashionable and supposedly progressive ideas, such as the Green New Deal.
title: Less is More: How Degrowth Will Save the World – Jason Hickel

author: Chris
description:
Keep your brain in great shape!

Discover the secrets of how the brain works and find out why sleep, exercise, diet, and even social interactions are so important for our health.

Focusing on key areas such as diet, sleep, exercise, brain training, and emotions, this book explains in simple terms the scientific basis of what really affects our brain, and provides practical tips and exercises to improve and support brain function at both younger and older ages.
title: The Power of the Brain. How to Live Healthier, Happier and Longer – Catherine de Lange

author: Chris
description:
Electrifying discoveries about a single chemical molecule in the brain that drives us to achieve the unattainable and distant – whether it concerns a flight to the Moon, a salt shaker on the other side of the table, or drawing closer to the absolute. This molecule compels us to pursue ever new goals. It is the source of creativity, and if we go too far – of madness.
LOVE: You've found the person you always waited for, so why doesn't the honeymoon last forever?
On the chemical molecules responsible for the desire for sex and falling in love – and why sooner or later everything becomes boring.
DRUGS: You crave thrills… but is that a good thing?
title: Molecule of More. How a Single Chemical in Your Brain Drives Love, Sex, and Creativity–and Will Determine the Fate of the Human – Daniel E. Lieberman, Michael E. Long

author: Chris
description:
If the conscious mind – the part we consider our "self" – is only the tip of the iceberg, what does the rest of the brain do?

In this brilliant and provocative book, renowned neurobiologist David Eagleman explores the depths of the subconscious brain to illuminate surprising mysteries.

Why is your foot already halfway to the brake pedal before you become aware of the danger ahead? Why do you hear your name in a conversation you didn't think you were listening to? What connects Ulysses to the credit crisis? Why did Thomas Edison electrocute an elephant in 1916?
title: Incognito: The Secret Lives of the Brain – David Eagleman

author: Chris
description:
Start working on your relationship with the help of an experienced family therapist.

In an age when toxic individualism permeates our society at every level, renowned author and respected couples therapist Terrence Real shows how our relationships suffer as a result. He observes that families fall victim to a culture that reinforces our dysfunctions.

The good news is: if we have the right tools, we can build a warmer, closer, more passionate relationship.

Us is a groundbreaking, science-based guide offering ways to become more collaborative. The author explains how to build a relationship full of empathy and closeness.
title: Us: Getting Past You and Me to Build a More Loving Relationship – Terrence Real

author: Chris
description:
A new book by the author of the bestseller "The Wisdom of Psychopaths."

The binary brain as a burden in a complex world

Ordering and categorizing is embedded in our instincts. We are programmed to divide and compartmentalize in a binary mode of black and white. That is simply how the human brain works. Immigrant or refugee? Muslim or Christian? Them or us?

Instead of reaching out to strangers, we draw closer to those who are similar to us. Instead of revising our perception of the world, we seek only to confirm what we already believe. As a result, the differences between extreme views grow even greater. And dangers lurk at every turn. ISIS. Racism. Brexit. Trump.
title: Black and White Thinking – Kevin Dutton

author: Chris
description:
Politicians, advertising specialists, self-proclaimed experts, salespeople, the media. People you trust. Also… You. All of us, consciously or not, stray from the truth.

Deceivers feed us simple stories. We fall into tribal "us versus them" thinking. Discussions become fruitless, polarization grows, and we reflexively reject differing opinions. We often deceive ourselves to feel that we "are right" and save face.

Are we doomed to a world where divisions grow ever deeper, discussions ever less substantive, differing views rejected without reflection, and objective truth ever less relevant?
title: We All Do IT, or a Short Story About Straying from the Truth – Dawid Myśliwiec

author: Chris
description:
Allergies, asthma, obesity, acne: these are just some of the conditions that may be caused – and one day cured – by the microscopic life inside us. The key is understanding how it affects our health, mood, and much more.

In recent years, scientists have shown that microscopic organisms in our bodies – particularly in the gut – have a remarkable significance for our lives. Health, mood, sleep patterns, eating habits – and even the likelihood of being bitten by mosquitoes – can all lead back to the intriguing creatures that live within us.
title: Follow Your Gut: The Enormous Impact of Tiny Microbes – Brendan Buhler, Rob Knight

author: Chris
description:
The rivalry between great powers is entering a critical phase.
Will the United States go to war with China? Whose side will Russia take? Will Poland be drawn into World War III? Does the world stand on the brink of nuclear annihilation?

These are just some of the questions Jacek Bartosiak and Piotr Zychowicz attempt to answer. The renowned geopolitician and historical commentator discuss Poland and the world. Whether the Polish army is ready to repel an attack and defend the state. September '39 must not repeat itself.

The United States is withdrawing from Europe to focus on the Pacific. And this means that American guarantees for Poland are becoming increasingly illusory.
title: World War III Is Coming. Will America Abandon Poland to Russia? – Jacek Bartosiak, Piotr Zychowicz

author: Chris
description:
I have been dealing with geopolitics, security and war for many years. Since February 2022, there has been warfare beyond Poland's eastern border, fundamentally changing the world and our region and directly affecting our security. We urgently need a strategy for Poland for these new, very turbulent times. We also need reflection on the quality of strategic culture in our country. That is what this book is about — the most personal one I have written so far. — Jacek Bartosiak

Jacek Bartosiak's latest publication is not devoted to the USA, China or Russia — it is a book about the Polish Republic, about what it is and what dreams we hold for it.
title: The Best Place in the World. Where East Collides with West – Jacek Bartosiak

author: Chris
description:
WHAT MAKES REASONABLE AND INTELLIGENT PEOPLE BELIEVE THE EARTH IS FLAT? AND WHY DO SOME NEVER CHANGE THEIR BELIEFS?

Here is a fascinating guide to contemporary neurobiological and psychological knowledge about forming and updating opinions.

David McRaney shows how to build connections, be mindful, and recognize the potential for change in others and in ourselves.

The author examines the latest research by psychologists and neurobiologists, revealing the limits of reasoning, the power of groupthink, and the results of deep persuasion.
title: How Minds Change: The Surprising Science of Belief, Opinion, and Persuasion – David McRaney
